column1: # comment: "GTS transport alignments. DCAT is the strongest RDF alignment: a GTS document is a distribution of a dataset/work. PROV-O aligns the compaction activity. The wire-format standards GTS builds on (CBOR, COSE, CDDL) and identifier schemes (IPLD CID) have no canonical RDF vocabularies; they are folded by reference in docs/GTS-SPEC.md and refused here (Principle 5)."
# # Loose / refused mappings (no canonical RDF vocabulary available):

column6: CBOR/RFC 8742 is a wire format, not an RDF vocabulary
content-addressing identifier scheme, not an RDF vocabulary
A compaction is a provenance activity: the compacted document prov:wasGeneratedBy it and prov:wasDerivedFrom the source document.
A GTS document is a concrete, downloadable embodiment of a dataset or work — DCAT's Distribution. Lossy: DCAT carries no segment structure, chain identity, or profile semantics.
A segment is a provenance entity with its own attribution (signers) and derivation history. Lossy: PROV carries no chain or head-identity semantics.
